activeLock.owner: The instance owner is always active.
activeLock.agent: An agent's account follows its agent.
activeLock.scim: Your identity provider (SCIM) decides which accounts are active.

users.deactivateBody: They are signed out at once and cannot sign in or use their API keys until you turn the account back on. Their MCP connections and the invites they sent are removed. Nothing else is deleted.

userPanel.unconfirmedHint: Confirm it here when the link never reached them.
userPanel.noAccessHint: This account reaches nothing until someone invites it to a project.
userPanel.deleteHint: Issues and comments stay, with the author unassigned.
userPanel.deleteConfirmWithProjects: {count, plural, one {Delete account and project} other {Delete account and projects}}
userPanel.deleteMessage: {name} loses access to this instance. Issues and comments they wrote stay, with the author unassigned. This cannot be undone.
userPanel.deleteWorkspaceNote: A workspace this account owns is deleted with it while it has no projects or AI agents. Otherwise it passes to you, with everything the account owned alone in it.
userPanel.soleOwnerTitle: {count, plural, one {Only owner of a project} other {Only owner of # projects}}
userPanel.soleOwnerHint: {count, plural, one {Once the account is gone, nobody can manage it.} other {Once the account is gone, nobody can manage them.}}
userPanel.deleteWithProjects: {count, plural, one {Delete the project with the account} other {Delete the projects with the account}}
userPanel.deleteWithProjectsOff: Or cancel and add a second owner first.

projectPanel.noMembersHint: Nobody can reach this project until someone is invited to it.

teamPanel.noProjectsHint: This team owns no projects yet.
teamPanel.noMembersHint: Nobody belongs to this team yet.

general.mcpEnabledHint: A new project is in its team's MCP reach from the moment it is created.
general.personalWorkspacesHint: Every account gets a workspace of its own, named after the person. Off, people work only in the workspaces they are added to.
general.traceRetentionHint: Each agent run records its model and tool calls. Usage dashboards count only the runs still kept.

authentication.registrationHint: Who may create an account on this instance.
authentication.inviteTtlDaysHint: After this many days an invite link stops working and, with invite-only registration, no longer lets its address sign up. 0 keeps invites valid until they are answered.
authentication.inviteTtlDaysInvalid: Enter a whole number of days from 0 to {max}.
authentication.allowedEmailDomainsHint: Only addresses at these domains can create an account. Separate them with commas, or leave empty to allow any. Existing accounts keep their access.
authentication.allowedEmailDomainsInvalid: Each domain should look like example.com, with up to 100 domains.

open.label: Open
open.description: Anyone who reaches the sign-up page can create an account.

invite.label: Invite only
invite.description: An account can only be created through an invite link.

closed.label: Closed
closed.description: No new accounts. Existing ones keep signing in.

authentication.signInHint: How people sign in. The options that send mail stay off until a provider is configured.
authentication.needsProvider: Set up the Email provider under Integrations first.
authentication.requireVerificationHint: A new account must confirm its address before it can sign in.
authentication.magicLinkHint: Offer signing in with a link sent by email, alongside the password.
authentication.trustProviderEmailsHint: Google and OpenID Connect sign a person in to the account that already has their address, confirmed here or not. Turn this on only where you control who can register at the provider.
authentication.emailPasswordHint: Offer the sign-in and sign-up form. Turn it off to let people in through a sign-in provider only.
authentication.needsSso: Set up a sign-in provider under Integrations first.

storage.fileSizeHint: The largest single file an upload may carry. A bigger file is refused before it is stored.
storage.attachmentHint: Applies to issue attachments, files pasted into a description, and attachments added by agents.
storage.avatarHint: The profile picture people upload for their account.
storage.mimeTypesHint: One content type per line. Leave empty to accept any file.
storage.mimeTypesNote: A line is a full type (application/pdf) or a wildcard (image/*). Files already stored are kept whatever the list says.
storage.quotaHint: Total attachment storage one project may use. 0 means no limit.
storage.quotaNote: Once a project reaches the quota, new uploads are refused until someone deletes attachments.

telegram.botConfigured: People connect their Telegram account by opening a chat with this bot from their profile.
telegram.botMissing: Create a bot with @BotFather in Telegram and paste its token here.
telegram.botTokenHint: The token is verified with Telegram when you save, so a wrong one is refused here rather than failing silently later.
telegram.resolvedHint: Resolved from the token. This is the bot people will see when connecting.

email.providerHint: Choose one provider. Credentials are stored encrypted.
email.fromHint: Required for Resend. With SMTP it defaults to the username.
email.teamNotificationsHint: Let teams deliver their notifications through this provider instead of configuring one of their own. Each team still chooses whether to use it.
email.testHint: Send a real message with the current settings without saving them.
email.testConfigureFirst: Enable a provider and add its required credentials first.
email.microsoft365Hint: Signs in as an app registration in Entra ID instead of with the mailbox password, so the mailbox can keep MFA on. The app needs the Office 365 Exchange Online application permission SMTP.SendAsApp with admin consent, access to this mailbox in Exchange, and SMTP AUTH turned on for the mailbox.
email.useInstanceAppHint: Sign in with the app set up under Microsoft 365 instead of separate credentials.

authProvider.googleConfigured: An address without an account gets one; an address that already has a confirmed account signs into it.
authProvider.googleMissing: Add the client ID and secret first.
authProvider.redirectUriHint: Register this on the OAuth client in the Google Cloud console. Google refuses the sign-in if it does not match exactly.
authProvider.oidcConfigured: An address without an account gets one; an address that already has a confirmed account signs into it.
authProvider.oidcMissing: Add the discovery URL, client ID and secret first.
authProvider.discoveryUrlHint: Your provider's .well-known/openid-configuration. The authorization, token and userinfo endpoints are read from it.
authProvider.oidcLabelHint: Names your provider on the sign-in button. Leave it empty for a generic label.
authProvider.scopesHint: Separated by spaces. openid is required; profile and email fill in the name and address.
authProvider.oidcRedirectUriHint: Register this as a redirect URI on the client at your identity provider. The provider refuses the sign-in if it does not match exactly.
authProvider.samlConfigured: An address without an account gets one; an address that already has a confirmed account signs into it.
authProvider.samlMissing: Add the identity provider metadata first.
authProvider.samlMetadataUrlHint: Your identity provider's metadata document. It is fetched once, when you save; save again to fetch a new version.
authProvider.samlMetadataXmlHint: Or paste the metadata document here instead of giving its URL.
authProvider.samlMetadataStored: Paste new metadata to replace the stored document
authProvider.samlMetadataSummary: Stored metadata for {entityId}, signing in at {ssoUrl}.
authProvider.samlEntityIdHint: The ID this instance gives the identity provider. Leave it empty to use the metadata URL below.
authProvider.samlEmailAttributeHint: The assertion attribute that holds the address. Empty uses email, then the NameID.
authProvider.samlNameAttributeHint: The attribute that holds the display name. Empty uses displayName. givenName and surname are used first when the provider sends them.
authProvider.samlAcsUrlHint: Register this as the assertion consumer service (reply URL) at your identity provider. It posts the signed response here.
authProvider.samlSpMetadataUrlHint: Most identity providers can read the entity ID and the ACS URL from this document. It answers once metadata is stored.
authProvider.ssoOnlyHint: Turn off password sign-in, so people sign in through an identity provider or with a passkey. The same switch as Password sign-in under Authentication.
authProvider.ssoOnlyNeedsProvider: Turn on a single sign-on provider first.

microsoft365.appHint: One Entra ID app registration for the whole instance. The secret is stored encrypted.
microsoft365.testHint: Request a Microsoft Graph token with these values without saving them.
microsoft365.testConfigureFirst: Enter the tenant ID, client ID and secret first.
microsoft365.reuseHint: Set it up once. These places can use it instead of credentials of their own.
microsoft365.reuseEmail: The email provider, when its authentication is Microsoft 365
microsoft365.reuseStorage: File storage on SharePoint or OneDrive
microsoft365.reuseAgents: Microsoft 365 credentials of team agent tools. The secret is never shown to team managers.

fileStorage.driverHint: Where attachments, avatars and skill files are stored. Changes apply to the api and the worker within seconds, without a restart.
fileStorage.warningTitle: Switching the driver does not move existing files
fileStorage.warningBody: Files already stored stay in the previous store and cannot be opened from the new one until they are copied.
fileStorage.copyHint: To copy every stored file from S3 to SharePoint, run this on a server that has the instance environment:
fileStorage.warningPending: The driver is about to change. Copy the files after saving.
fileStorage.s3Hint: Used while the driver is S3.
fileStorage.sharepointHint: Used while the driver is SharePoint. Files are written under the root folder of one document library.
fileStorage.inactiveHint: Not in use. Saved here so it is ready when you switch the driver.
fileStorage.endpointHint: A private address such as http://minio:9000 is accepted only when it equals the S3_ENDPOINT environment variable or is listed in STORAGE_ALLOWED_PRIVATE_HOSTS.
fileStorage.forcePathStyleHint: Needed for RustFS, MinIO and most self-hosted stores. Turn it off for stores that only serve virtual-host-style buckets.
fileStorage.useInstanceAppHint: Take the tenant, client and secret from the Microsoft 365 section instead of entering them here.
fileStorage.instanceAppMissing: The instance Microsoft 365 app is not set up yet.
fileStorage.siteHint: Give the site ID or the drive ID.
fileStorage.willUseEnvironment: The environment value is used after saving
fileStorage.testHint: Writes, reads and deletes a small probe object with the values above, without saving them.

procore.title: Procore
procore.hint: Reads projects, punch items and RFIs with a Developer Managed Service Account. Nothing is written to Procore.
procore.projectIdHint: Optional. The first project listed is used when empty.
procore.rememberHint: Stored encrypted so the next check needs no typing. Without it nothing is kept.

sharepoint.title: SharePoint storage
sharepoint.hint: Writes, reads and deletes test files, including one large enough for an upload session, with the saved file storage settings.

microsoft365.title: Microsoft 365 tools
microsoft365.hint: Runs the read-only agent tools (files, mail, calendar, teams) through the instance Microsoft 365 app.
microsoft365.write: Also write and read back a test file in that user's OneDrive
microsoft365.writeHint: The file stays in an itsaplan-verify folder, because the tools cannot delete.

allowedOrigins.title: Allowed sign-in addresses
allowedOrigins.hint: Web addresses people may open this app from, in addition to the one set by the environment. Others are refused at sign-in and by the api.
allowedOrigins.extraHint: One per line, as scheme, host and optional port. A wildcard is allowed only as the first label of the host, for example http://*.orca.localhost:60418.
